sentences.text: Lewisuchus was a small archosaur, a group of reptiles closely related to dinosaurs, that measured about one meter in length.
Its back was protected by osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin that formed a type of armor.
A specimen found in 2013 and described in 2019 provided crucial evidence that Pseudolagosuchus major and Lewisuchus admixtus are the same species.

The first remains were uncovered during a 1964–1965 joint expedition by the Museo de La Plata and Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology. Alfred Romer named the genus in 1972 based on a partial skeleton catalogued as 64-XI-14-14. The name Lewisuchus honors Arnold D. Lewis, the preparator who discovered the holotype skeleton.
Fossils of Lewisuchus have been found in the Chañares Formation of Argentina. The animal lived between 241.464 and 233.6 million years ago, spanning the Ladinian to Carnian stages.
A 2014 study refrained from synonymizing Pseudolagosuchus major with Lewisuchus admixtus due to insufficient overlapping fossil data.
